- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early/medium horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast, particularly if recent price is falling.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or adjust downward by 0.5–1.5 units.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch the reversal; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.0 units in the next 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >1.5σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.3–0.7 units; if below, increase by 0.3–0.7 units.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment; dampen by 0.2–0.5 units if sentiment is noisy or mixed.
- If sentiment is flat (0.33–0.67) for 3+ days, model tends to drift; apply smoothing or add 0.1–0.3 units to forecast to avoid underestimation.
